sentences.zh: 挑战似乎总是要与特朗普竞争，成为这场竞选中新气象和变革的化身。

sentences.en: Well, I think Harris benefits from the fact that she hasn't been president before, and she is not 80 years old, nor a man, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为哈里斯受益于她以前没有当过总统的事实，而且她不是80岁，也不是男性，对吧？

sentences.en: I think that all of those things—
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些事情——

sentences.en: That's change.
sentences.zh: 那就是变革。

sentences.en: —all of those things represent a change in the office that wouldn't have been there before.
sentences.zh: ——所有这些都代表了办公室的一种变革，这是以前不存在的。

sentences.en: I think the poll is a reflection of a premise that Democrats and the Biden-turned-Harris
sentences.zh: 我认为这次民调反映了一个前提，即民主党和拜登转哈里斯

sentences.en: campaign has had for a while, which is that as this election will get closer, people will get
sentences.zh: 竞选团队已经有一段时间了，那就是随着选举临近，人们会变得

sentences.en: more scared about Donald Trump, and that issues like abortion will become more tangible to folks
sentences.zh: 更害怕唐纳德·特朗普，像堕胎这样的议题会变得对人们更具体，

sentences.en: and rise on their priority list, particularly in those battlegrounds that we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 并在他们的优先事项列表中上升，特别是在我们谈论的那些摇摆州。

sentences.en: And so I think if you're the Harris campaign, that's been the card that you've been trying to play the whole time.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为如果你是哈里斯竞选团队，这就是你一直试图打出的牌。

sentences.en: I think right now, they're basically running the playbook they want.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在，他们基本上是在执行他们想要的剧本。

sentences.en: And so I think if you look at that poll and you're them, there are signs that it could be quote-unquote working, but I think it still presumes 51-49.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看那份民调，如果你是他们，有迹象表明它可能在起作用，但我认为它仍然预设了51-49的局面。

sentences.en: And what's wrong with that presumption or right about it?
sentences.zh: 这种预设有什么问题或正确之处吗？

sentences.en: I guess, like, we're talking about differences in the degree.
sentences.zh: 我想，我们是在讨论程度上的差异。

sentences.en: Like, so I don't really have a great answer for you because I don't know if she has landed the brand of change candidate.
sentences.zh: 所以，我其实给不出一个完美的答案，因为我不知道她是否已经成功树立了“变革候选人”的品牌形象。

sentences.en: I think as of right now, she is doing better with the electorate on that specific question.
sentences.zh: 我认为就目前而言，在那个具体问题上，她在选民中的表现要好一些。

sentences.en: But I think that's the question that this all hinges on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这正是这一切所悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: No, I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 不，我同意这一点。

sentences.en: Sted is absolutely right.
sentences.zh: Sted说得完全正确。

sentences.en: We are seeing the Biden-Harris theory of the case congealing to some extent, right?
sentences.zh: 我们看到拜登-哈里斯的竞选理论在某种程度上正在成形，对吧？

sentences.en: That basically, this is the later stage of a general election.
sentences.zh: 基本上，现在是大选的后期阶段了。

sentences.en: A lot of voters have not been tuned in.
sentences.zh: 很多选民一直没怎么关注。

sentences.en: A lot of people have tuned out of politics to a great extent since 2020 and are now paying more attention just in this final stage.
sentences.zh: 自2020年以来，很多人在很大程度上已经不再关注政治，只是在最后这个阶段才开始多加留意。

sentences.en: But what it means, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 但这到底意味着什么，我不知道。

sentences.en: Nate would be much smarter on this than I am.
sentences.zh: 在这方面，Nate会比我聪明得多。

sentences.en: He's smarter than all of us.
sentences.zh: 他比我们所有人都聪明。

sentences.en: Well, on everything, really, but certainly on what I'm about to say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实在所有事情上都是，但肯定包括我接下来要说的这件事。

sentences.en: There is a scenario that some pollsters have privately described to me where Harris could win the popular vote by a smaller margin than Biden or Hillary Clinton did.
sentences.zh: 有一些民调专家私下向我描述过一种情况，即哈里斯赢得普选票的优势可能会比拜登或希拉里·克林顿当年要小。

sentences.en: But still eke out a victory in the battlegrounds.
sentences.zh: 但她仍然可以在摇摆州险胜。

sentences.en: And that is not something we have seen before.
sentences.zh: 这在以前是我们从未见过的。

sentences.en: But, Nate, tell me if you think I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 不过，Nate，如果你觉得我说错了，请告诉我。

sentences.en: I don't think you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你错了。

sentences.en: And I think our Florida poll is part of that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们的佛罗里达州民调就是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Just explain that because we just talked about how Florida is no longer a swing state.
sentences.zh: 解释一下吧，因为我们刚才还在讨论佛罗里达州已经不再是摇摆州了。

sentences.en: So why do you keep referring to Florida as if it's somehow revealing?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么一直提到佛罗里达州，好像它能说明什么问题似的？

sentences.en: Well, Maggie mentioned that Harris might do worse than prior Democratic candidates in non-competitive states while holding up in the core battlegrounds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Maggie提到哈里斯在非竞争性州可能会比之前的民主党候选人表现更差，同时在核心摇摆州保持住优势。

sentences.en: If that were to be true,
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，

sentences.en: you would expect to see polls where Donald Trump's doing pretty darn well in a state like Florida where he will rack up additional votes in the popular vote but no additional electoral votes.
sentences.zh: 你会预料到在佛罗里达州这样的地方，唐纳德·特朗普的表现会相当不错，他会在普选票中获得额外的选票，但不会增加选举人票。

sentences.en: In the Electoral College, it doesn't matter whether Trump wins Florida by 3 or 14.
sentences.zh: 在选举人团制度下，特朗普是以3个百分点还是14个百分点赢得佛罗里达州并不重要。

sentences.en: But if you make a 10-point gain in Florida, if you make a 10-point gain in New York where the polls also show Donald Trump doing very well,
sentences.zh: 但如果你在佛罗里达州获得了10个百分点的增长，如果你在纽约州也获得了10个百分点的增长——民调也显示唐纳德·特朗普在那里表现非常好——

sentences.en: those two states alone shave a whole point off of Harris's potential lead in the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 单单这两个州就能让哈里斯在普选票中的潜在领先优势缩水整整一个百分点。

sentences.en: And there could be other states out there like that.
sentences.zh: 而且可能还有其他类似的州。

sentences.en: But one thing that I think we saw in the 2022 midterm election is that the issues of the last few years, starting with the coronavirus, the backlash against woke, crime,
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们在2022年中期选举中看到的一点是，过去几年的议题，从新冠疫情开始，到对“觉醒文化”的反弹、犯罪、

sentences.en: immigration, abortion, January 6th, all these issues were felt very differently in different parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 移民、堕胎、1月6日事件，所有这些议题在全国不同地区感受非常不同。

sentences.en: We saw Florida go to the right.
sentences.zh: 我们看到佛罗里达州向右转。

sentences.en: We saw Pennsylvania go to the left in the midterm election.
sentences.zh: 我们看到宾夕法尼亚州在中期选举中向左转。

sentences.en: And I think we – I, at least at the time, interpreted that as about the issues that the particular candidates were running on.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们——至少我当时——将其解读为与特定候选人所竞选的议题有关。

sentences.en: And I think that as more polls come out in this general election, it seems like it was more than that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为随着这次大选更多民调出炉，情况似乎不仅仅如此。

sentences.en: It seems like the upheaval in American life after the pandemic and during the pandemic had a lasting impact on different parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 似乎疫情之后以及疫情期间美国生活的动荡对全国不同地区产生了持久的影响。

sentences.en: And that may mitigate Harris's advantage in the popular vote.
sentences.zh: 这可能会削弱哈里斯在普选票中的优势。

sentences.en: And it may not do as much in the battleground states,
sentences.zh: 而且在摇摆州可能不会有那么大的影响，

sentences.en: especially if something like Donald Trump trying to steal the last election left a bigger mark on the people whose votes were trying to be flipped.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果像唐纳德·特朗普试图窃取上次选举结果这样的事情，对那些选票曾被试图篡改的人群留下了更深的印记的话。

sentences.en: I just want to make sure I understand what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保我理解了你的意思。

sentences.en: Trump could be doing better and better in a place like Florida and seemingly leave Kamala Harris in the duSt.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在佛罗里达州这样的地方可能会表现得越来越好，看起来把卡玛拉·哈里斯甩在了身后。

sentences.en: And you're saying don't mistake that for actually meaning she's struggling in the battleground states.
sentences.zh: 而你的意思是，不要误以为这意味着她在摇摆州表现挣扎。

sentences.en: She might still be doing better there because culturally, politically, they are just less likely to drift into some of these more extreme swings.
sentences.zh: 她可能在那里表现依然更好，因为在文化和政治上，这些州不太可能出现某些更极端的摇摆。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为你说得对。

sentences.en: And I don't – I actually think that some of it's about the way that these states experienced the pandemic and its aftermath.
sentences.zh: 而且我不——我其实认为这部分与这些州经历疫情及其后果的方式有关。

sentences.en: Floridians came out of that experience apparently being much more skeptical of the views of the establishment left.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达人从那段经历中走出来时，显然对建制派左翼的观点持更加怀疑的态度。

sentences.en: And the same experience didn't happen in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 而宾夕法尼亚州并没有发生同样的经历。

sentences.en: And in fact, they may have had the exact opposite takeaway from their experiences there.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们从那里的经历中得出的结论可能恰恰相反。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: And I think that all of this may have happened long before the election given that we saw all of this in the midterms where the Republicans have won the House popular vote but nearly lost the House.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这一切可能在大选前很久就已经发生了，因为我们在中期选举中就看到了这一切，当时共和党赢得了众议院的普选票，但几乎输掉了众议院。

sentences.en: I want to talk about how Kamala Harris is trying to win these battleground states where her chances seem relatively good.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈卡玛拉·哈里斯是如何试图赢得这些她胜算相对较大的摇摆州的。

sentences.en: She went on a uncharacteristic media blitz this past week.
sentences.zh: 过去一周，她进行了一场不同寻常的媒体闪电战。

sentences.en: Daddy gang, I went to Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: “Daddy Gang”（播客听众名），我去了华盛顿特区

sentences.en: to interview Vice President Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 采访副总统卡玛拉·哈里斯。

sentences.en: Welcome back to All the Smoke.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《All the Smoke》节目。

sentences.en: We got a very special guest today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们有一位非常特别的嘉宾。

sentences.en: Very excited to sit down and talk to Miss Madam Vice President Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 非常高兴能坐下来与卡玛拉·哈里斯副总统交谈。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It is so good to be with you.
sentences.zh: 能和你在一起真是太好了。

sentences.en: Thank you for sitting down with us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: It feels immodest to me to talk about myself, which apparently I'm doing right now.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，谈论自己感觉有点不谦虚，尽管我显然正在这么做。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But you have to, right?
sentences.zh: 但你必须这么做，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, you do.
sentences.zh: 是的，你必须这样做。

sentences.en: You're running for office.
sentences.zh: 你在竞选公职。

sentences.en: I said I want to talk about why she went on this media blitz.
sentences.zh: 我说过我想谈谈她为什么进行这场媒体闪电战。

sentences.en: A lot has been made of the shows that she chose to go on.
sentences.zh: 她选择参加的节目引起了很多议论。

sentences.en: Obviously, The Daily was not one of them.
sentences.zh: 显然，《The Daily》不在其中。

sentences.en: Or the run-up.
sentences.zh: 或者《The Run-Up》节目。

sentences.en: Or the run-up.
sentences.zh: 或者《The Run-Up》节目。

sentences.en: Her loss.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的损失。

sentences.en: Invitations lost in the mail.
sentences.zh: 邀请函寄丢了。

sentences.en: But I think it's important to note that each of them had a very specific constituency, but then also to just kind of tackle the totality of what she's up to.
sentences.zh: 但我认为值得注意的是，每一个节目都有非常特定的受众群体，同时也需要从整体上审视她正在做的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think you're referring to her recent appearances on the Call Her Daddy podcast and also All the Smoke that she did.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想你指的是她最近参加的《Call Her Daddy》播客，还有她做的《All the Smoke》节目。

sentences.en: Not to mention The View and The Colbert Show.
sentences.zh: 更不用说《The View》和《Colbert Show》了。

sentences.en: The View, Colbert Show.
sentences.zh: 《观点》节目，科尔伯特秀。

sentences.en: Howard Stern.
sentences.zh: 霍华德·斯特恩（Howard Stern）。

sentences.en: Howard Stern.
sentences.zh: 霍华德·斯特恩。

sentences.en: Howard Stern.
sentences.zh: 霍华德·斯特恩。

sentences.en: I think it is clear that the Harris campaign sees this effort as their attempts to win low propensity voters.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，哈里斯竞选团队将此举视为他们争取低投票倾向选民的尝试。

sentences.en: Low propensity meaning not likely to vote.
sentences.zh: 低投票倾向意味着不太可能去投票。

sentences.en: Not likely to vote.
sentences.zh: 不太可能去投票。

sentences.en: And so I think that the media strategy reflects a core belief of what the campaign has been saying
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这种媒体策略反映了竞选团队长期以来所坚持的核心信念，

sentences.en: for a long time, which is they don't think traditional and mass media are the ways that they reach those people.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们认为传统媒体和大众媒体并不是接触那些人的途径。

sentences.en: And so I don't think it's surprising that in the final month, they're really ramping up some of those appearances.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在最后一个月，他们真正加大这些节目的曝光度并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I guess I think, like, these things work on multiple fronts.
sentences.zh: 我想，这些事情在多个层面都在起作用。

sentences.en: Like, I think some of the journalists whining about it are just being whiny, like, because about access and stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如，我认为一些抱怨此事的记者只是在发牢骚，因为涉及采访权限之类的问题。

sentences.en: Hardly the first time.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是第一次了。

sentences.en: Like, you know, like, I think, like, we could call some of our people out.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，我认为我们可以指出我们自己人的一些问题。

sentences.en: Like, it's been ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: But I also think that we can't act like this is just a good faith effort on their part.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为我们不能表现得好像这仅仅是他们出于好意的努力。

sentences.en: Like, it makes a lot of sense of why they're doing the shows.
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要做这些节目，这很有道理。

sentences.en: But this comes as they've done less and less of traditional media.
sentences.zh: 但这发生在她越来越少参与传统媒体活动的情况下。

sentences.en: And so when we see a Harris candidate have electorate saying they don't know a lot about her or that they wish that her policy was more fleshed out, some of that, I think, is a
sentences.zh: 所以当我们看到哈里斯的选民说他们对她了解不多，或者希望她的政策更具体时，我认为其中一些是

sentences.en: response to not feeling like they've got some of those more traditional answers.
sentences.zh: 对没能从传统渠道获得那些答案的一种反应。

sentences.en: And so I guess I'm saying I understand why they're doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我想说的是，我理解他们为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: But I also don't think it solves a core problem.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为这并不能解决核心问题。

sentences.en: It is an attempt to reach a different type of audience.
sentences.zh: 这是一种接触不同类型受众的尝试。

sentences.en: But turning those people into voters is only one thing they have to do.
sentences.zh: 但将这些人转化为选民只是他们必须做的事情之一。

sentences.en: Answering the core questions about her beliefs and ideology is another thing they have to do.
sentences.zh: 回答关于她的信仰和意识形态的核心问题是他们必须做的另一件事。

sentences.en: And so I think that the nontraditional stops succeed on the former but don't really help the latter.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为非传统媒体的曝光在前者上取得了成功，但对后者并没有太大帮助。

sentences.en: Nate, you and I have talked about this concept that for quite some time Kamala Harris avoided what felt like a lot of opportunities to tell a story of her candidacy.
sentences.zh: Nate，你和我讨论过这个概念，即卡玛拉·哈里斯长期以来回避了许多讲述她竞选故事的机会。

sentences.en: And this clearly seemed like a corrective.
sentences.zh: 而这显然看起来是一种纠正。

sentences.en: And one thing that you said to me, I think it was last week we were just chit-chatting,
sentences.zh: 你对我说的有一件事，我想是上周我们闲聊时说的，

sentences.en: you talked about the value of just giving people something to attach themselves to about a candidate, which, of course, Donald Trump has done for years.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了给人们提供一些可以与候选人建立联系的东西的价值，这当然是唐纳德·特朗普多年来一直在做的。

sentences.en: In watching some of these interviews that Kamala Harris did, I found what seemed like ample opportunities to grab hold of some humanity.
sentences.zh: 在观看卡玛拉·哈里斯做的一些采访时，我发现有很多机会可以展现她的人性化一面。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of the moment that Stephen Colbert asked her to look at a portrait of herself with her hand under her chin from the first debate with Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想到斯蒂芬·科尔伯特让她看一张她在与唐纳德·特朗普第一次辩论时手托下巴的照片的那一刻。

sentences.en: This moment went viral from the debate.
sentences.zh: 这一瞬间在辩论后疯传。

sentences.en: Can you tell us what you're thinking at this moment right here?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们你当时在想什么吗？

sentences.en: And he asked her, you know, what were you thinking in this now iconic photo?
sentences.zh: 他问她，你知道，在这张现在标志性的照片里你在想什么？

sentences.en: And she had a very funny answer.
sentences.zh: 她给出了一个非常有趣的回答。

sentences.en: She said,
sentences.zh: 她说，

sentences.en: It's family TV, right?
sentences.zh: 这是家庭电视节目，对吧？

sentences.en: It starts with a W.
sentences.zh: 它以W开头。

sentences.en: There's a letter between and then the last letter is F.
sentences.zh: 中间有一个字母，最后一个字母是F。

sentences.en: And that is a changed strategy from the kind of more bunkered Kamala Harris that I think you and I were talking about when we had that conversation.
sentences.zh: 这与我们上次谈话时提到的那种更加“深挖洞”的卡玛拉·哈里斯相比，是一种改变了的策略。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are a lot of different ways that a candidate can forge a real connection with a voter, much in the same way as we can all have different bases for our friendships.
sentences.zh: 是的，候选人与选民建立真正联系的方式有很多种，就像我们所有人建立友谊的基础可以各不相同一样。

sentences.en: Like we could like shared activities or we can enjoy our someone's intellect or be competitive.
sentences.zh: 比如我们可以喜欢共同的活动，或者我们可以欣赏某人的才智，或者具有竞争性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。
